description.narrative: A national system for the notification and recording of work-related accidents and injuries developed by the Ministry of Labour. The system, which is available for the first time in the country, is based on workplace reports of work related accidents and injuries. It will improve data collection and will provide regular information to in designing workplace intervention for each areas of concern. The ILO provided technical guidance and training on improving notification and reporting system on work injuries for labour inspectors. The ILO also facilitated awareness raising on the importance of the notification and recording system on work related accidents and injuries for social partners.

description.narrative: Establishment of new General Directorate of Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) was approved by the Cabinet in April 2021. An annual plan of action for improving OSH at the national level was developed and implemented for 2021. The National Tripartite Committee on OSH developed and adopted a national OSH profile, including Gaza, in April 2021. Following the OSH profile, the Ministry of Labour drafted a national OSH policy and strategy in November 2021, and finalized, based on discussions with the social partners, in December 2021. The national OSH policy and programme focus on preventing occupational diseases and cover main areas of OSH in construction and the identification and reporting of occupational diseases. They will also promote effective planning, evidence-based OSH inspection and strengthening OSH committees at the enterprise level. The ILO provided technical support for developing detailed terms of reference and job description for the new OSH Directorate and its staff. The ILO reviewed the national OSH profile and provided technical guidance on key areas for improvement, namely in addressing OSH deficits in key economic sectors and building preventative OSH culture. The ILO has also provided training for government officials and social partners on promoting occupational health services at the enterprise level, including establishment of OSH committees and appointment of qualified OSH supervisors.

description.narrative: The Ministry of Labour conducted an assessment of the national labour inspection system, including in the West Bank and Gaza, in February 2021, and developed and implemented an action plan for enhancing labour inspection effectiveness in line with the relevant ILS. The ILO provided technical guidance in conducting the assessment and advice on how to align the action plan with relevant international labour standards, in particular Labour Inspection Convention, 1947 (No. 81) and Labour Inspection (Agriculture) Convention, 1969 (No.129).

description.narrative: The first National Social Dialogue Conference, held in March 2021, resulted in the increase of the national minimum wage from 1,450 to 1,880 Israeli Shekels per month, to be effectively implemented from 1 January 2022. With technical support from the ILO to the Palestinian Authority and the social partners, the first National Social Dialogue Conference, 3-4 March 2021, allowed for extensive consultations with workers and employers to arrive at consensus on the increase of the national minimum wage. The ILO also supported the work on the minimum wage through a data-based technical review study of the minimum wage in the occupied Palestinian territory, carried out in 2019, followed by a workshop to present the findings to the National Wage Committee. The ILO has supported reforms of the labour law that are imperative for addressing labour market inequalities and the realization of labour rights.

description.narrative: The labour inspectorates adopted and started implementing the Strategic Compliance Plan for kindergarten sector, covering the issues of minimum wage, unpaid wage, leave violations and overtime payments. To monitor implementation, the labour inspectorate established an internal working group – the Strategic Compliance Task Team – that meets regularly. The plan assists the labour inspectorate to improve deliver in collaboration with other actors. The inspectorate was initially able to identify approximately 100 kindergartens from their internal enterprise list. Through collaboration with the Ministry of Education, which licenses educational institutions, the labour inspectorate identified and targeted 819 economic units for inspection. Inspections began in October to coincide with the start of the school year. The Strategic Compliance Plan in Palestine is well underway including 100% of the communication intervention, 80% of the systemic intervention , and 25% of the enforcement intervention. The ILO organized a strategic compliance planning workshop and provided technical advice in developing strategic interventions, namely the enforcement, systemic and communication interventions. As part of the communication intervention, the Strategic Compliance Task Team of the labour inspectorate, with assistance from the ILO, developed and printed a complaint card with information on how and where to submit complaints to the labour inspectorate and an informational brochure on labour rights and duties for kindergarten staff. Both are being distributed during the inspection campaign.

description.narrative: Tripartite social dialogue in OPT has been strengthened. The National Tripartite Labour Policies Committee (NTLPC) is facilitating tripartite social dialogue on several key policy issues, such as reform to labour law, social security legislation, sectoral bargaining and labour dispute mechanisms. Moreover, it has also facilitated the negotiation and tripartite adoption of the National Employment Strategy, which was launched officially on 3 March 2021 on the occasion of the High Level social dialogue conference. ILO supported the social dialogue conference in March 2021, which was a great success as it did not only strengthen tripartite social dialogue, but it also led to an agreement on the increase of the minimum wage and resumption of dialogue on reforms to labour law and social security legislation. The ILO supported technically the tripartite and inter-ministerial committee in holding extensive thematic consultations and the development of the National Employment Strategy (2021-2025). The ILO undertook a study on social dialogue processes and mechanisms in OPT – a first of its kind – that contains concrete set of recommendations on strengthening capacity, restructuring the NTLPC and activing local/sectoral dialogue in key areas.
